title: A Second Demonstration of Correlation Analysis in Python and Quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd 
import numpy as np 

import seaborn as sns

sns.set_context('talk')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = sns.load_dataset('diamonds')

The diamonds dataset form seaborn offers a great opportunity to learn more about correlation analysis in Python and Quarto where we will be working with data from 53940 diamonds and our research question is to study whether the carat of the diamond is correlated with the depth of the diamond.


Literature Review


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data (carat of diomand and depth of diamond), we will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['carat', 'depth']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > 0.8:
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a weak positive correlation" 
elif corr_val > -0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the classic simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.02822, so we conclude the relationship is a weak positive correlation.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'depth', x = 'carat')

plt.ylabel('Depth')
plt.xlabel('Carat')







Figure 1: A scatterplot of diamond carat and depth





As shown in Figure 1 we see additional evidence of a weak positive correlative relationship.


Discussion
Now we know how to do correlation coefficient analysis from this example work-through of the diamond dataset using Python and Quarto and we have found a weak positive correlative relationship.
